account: Task: Fix MultilineContinuationError doc in Doc/library/configparser.rst per reviewer findings. (1) Say 'indented more deeply than the preceding option line' not just 'an indented continuation line'; note blank/comment lines don't trigger. (2) source defaults to '<string>' for string input (not a replacement); line may lack final newline. (3) Remove .. versionadded:: 3.12. Then check and submit.
discussion: I need to fix three issues in the MultilineContinuationError documentation: (1) distinguish relative greater indentation and account for blank/comment processing, (2) source is a default not a replacement, line may lack final newline, (3) remove the unsupported versionadded 3.12. I have the current doc text visible in the working set. Let me apply the patch.

operation.new:
.. exception:: MultilineContinuationError

   Raised when a line indented more deeply than the preceding option
   line follows a valueless option (an option with no value, as
   permitted by ``allow_no_value=True``).  Blank lines and comment
   lines are processed before the continuation check and do not
   trigger this exception.  This is a subclass of
   :exc:`!ParsingError`.

   The constructor takes three arguments: ``source`` (the name of the
   source being parsed, defaulting to ``'<string>'`` for string input
   when no source name is supplied), ``lineno`` (the one-based line
   number of the offending continuation line), and ``line`` (the raw
   text of the offending line, which may lack a final newline).
   All three values are stored as attributes of the same name and
   are preserved in ``args`` for pickling and copying.

   .. attribute:: source

   .. attribute:: lineno

   .. attribute:: line
operation.old:
.. exception:: MultilineContinuationError

   Raised when an indented continuation line follows a valueless option
   (an option with no value, as permitted by ``allow_no_value=True``).
   This is a subclass of :exc:`!ParsingError`.

   The constructor takes three arguments: ``source`` (the name of the
   source being parsed, or ``'<string>'`` for string input), ``lineno``
   (the one-based line number of the offending continuation line), and
   ``line`` (the exact text of that line, including its trailing
   newline).  All three values are stored as attributes of the same
   name and are preserved in ``args`` for pickling and copying.

   .. attribute:: source

   .. attribute:: lineno

   .. attribute:: line

   .. versionadded:: 3.12
